newsitem.title: USA: Vermont says jobless rate eases 0.01 to 4.4 in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Vermont says jobless rate eases 0.01 to 4.4 in Dec.

text.p: Vermont on Tuesday said that the unemployment rate fell 0.01 percentage point to 4.4 percent in December, mainly due to a rise in holiday activities, as the skiing industry declined from a year-ago.
In the state's 13 labor markets, unemployment rates ranged from 1.8 percent in Hartford-Lebanon to 9.0 percent in Newport, though these data were not seasonally adjusted.

Employment rose 1,000 in December, but this was mainly due to unusual job levels at state educational institutions, which might be due to changes in the academic calender, the state labor department said, in a prepared statement.
The service industry added 300 jobs, mainly for holiday activiites, as unfavorable weather during much of December might have hurt ski resorts.
While the lodging industry added nearly 2,500 jobs, rebounding to its highest level, retail trade grew 850, about 1,000 above last year, the state agency said.
Manufacturing and construction, however, did not add workers, while total nonfarm job growth for the year was 1.5 percent, nearly matching last month, it added.
